Dated 2021
THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SALFORD
– and –
HILTON STREET DEVELOPMENTS (MANCHESTER) LIMITED
- and -
TOGETHER COMMERCIAL FINANCE LIMITED
and others
Agreement
pursuant to section 106 of the Town and
Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended)
relating to 311-315 Bury New Road
Salford M7 2YN
City Solicitor
P O Box 532
Town Hall
Albert Square
Manchester
M60 2LA

This Agreement is made the day of
Between:
(1) THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SALFORD of Salford Civic Centre, Chorley
Road, Swinton, Manchester M27 5DA (the “Council”);
(2) HILTON STREET DEVELOPMENTS (MANCHESTER) LIMITED (incorporated
in England with company number 11725496) whose registered office is at
Abacus Solicitors, Reedham House, 31-33 King Street West, Manchester, M3
2PN (the “Owner”);
(3) TOGETHER COMMERCIAL FINANCE LIMITED (incorporated in England with
company number 02058813) whose registered office is at Lake View, Lakeside,
Cheadle, Cheshire, SK8 3GW (the “First Mortgagee”);
(4) ECS CAPITAL LIMITED (incorporated in England with company number
08769874) whose registered office is at Kay Johnson Gee Llp, 2nd Floor, 1 City
Road East, Manchester, M15 4PN and ANDREW HIGGINSON care of Abacus
Solicitors, Reedham House, 31-33 King Street West, Manchester, M3 2PN
(together the “Second Mortgagee”);
(5) ECS CAPITAL LIMITED (incorporated in England with company number
08769874) whose registered office is at Kay Johnson Gee Llp, 2nd Floor, 1 City
Road East, Manchester, M15 4PN and APPLE P.P.E. LIMITED (incorporated in
England with company number 05901292) whose registered office is at Vernon
House, 40 New North Road, Huddersfield, West Yorkshire, HD1 5LS (together
the “Third Mortgagee”);
Background
A The Council is the local planning authority for the purposes of the Act in relation
to the Site and is the authority by whom the obligations hereby created are
enforceable. The Development will be carried out on the Site. The Site is situated
within the administrative boundaries of Salford and this planning obligation is
enforceable by the Council.
B The Owner is the freehold owner of the Site registered at the Land Registry with
Title Absolute under Title Numbers GM813338, GM388032 and LA103094 and
Possessory Title under Title Number MAN332903 together with but subject to all
matters contained or referred to in the Title Registers thereunder.
C The First Mortgagee is interested in the Site by virtue of the Together Legal
Charges as defined herein.
D The Second Mortgagee is interested in the Site by virtue of a legal charge and a
Debenture both dated 28 May 2020 (the “Second Mortgagee’s Charges”).
E The Third Mortgagee is interested in the Site by virtue of a legal charge and a
Debenture both dated 28 May 2020 (the “Third Mortgagee’s Charges”).
F The Application was submitted to the Council for planning permission to carry out
the Development in the manner set out in the plans, specifications and particulars
submitted as part of the Application. The Council as local planning authority is
satisfied that the Development is such as may be approved by the Council under
the Act and is minded to grant planning permission for the Development in
accordance with the Application but having considered the SPD and the
Regulations is desirous of the Owner entering into this Agreement without which
planning permission would not be granted.
G The SPD sets out a requirement to provide a contribution towards meeting
expenditure relating to open space provision. The Council has identified a need
to direct the contribution towards the purposes set out in Schedule 4. The
application of the SPD to the Development means that there is also a
requirement to provide affordable housing on the Site in the manner hereinafter
appearing in this Agreement. The Council has determined that the Development
in order to comply with the SPD will support the payment of the Open Space
Contribution as defined herein and the provision of affordable housing in the
manner hereinafter appearing.
H The Owner has agreed to enter into this Agreement in support of the Application
so as to create planning obligations in favour of the Council pursuant to section
106 of the Act with the intention that the planning obligations contained in this
Agreement are binding upon the Site and may, subject to the provisions of this
Agreement, be enforced by the Council against the Owner and its successors in
title.
I The Council and the Owner agree that the Open Space Contribution is needed for
and may be used for any of the purposes specified in Schedule 4 of this
Agreement any of which purposes meet the criteria set out in subparagraphs (a)
to (c) of Recital K in this background section of this Agreement and in any event
are acceptable as using the Open Space Contribution for any of those purposes
will provide a planning benefit to the area in the vicinity of the Development.
J The planning purpose of this Agreement is to improve the amenity of land in the
locality of the Site with benefit for the occupiers of the Development and to
mitigate the adverse impacts of the Development in accordance with the
development plan for the area and other material considerations. In addition the
Council has recognised the difficulty faced by lower income groups in buying
homes within the Administrative Boundaries of Salford and aims to increase the
provision of affordable housing within the Administrative Boundaries of Salford
and the Owner has agreed to make provision for affordable housing in the
manner hereinbefore and hereinafter appearing.
K The Council is satisfied that the obligations in this Agreement are;
(a) necessary to make the Development acceptable in planning terms (including
where appropriate, obligations necessary to mitigate the adverse impacts of
the Development in accordance with the development plan for the area and
other material considerations);
(b) directly related to the Development; and
(c) fairly and reasonably related in scale and kind to the Development
and in any event will secure other planning benefits.
Agreed Terms
Definitions and Interpretation
1.1 The definitions and rules of interpretation set out in this Clause apply to this
Agreement.
“Act” the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended by the Planning and
Compensation Act 1991 and the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 and
the Planning Act 2008;
“Anticipated Date of Completion of Construction” means the date upon which
the Owner anticipate that the Completion of Construction of the relevant
percentage of Dwellings referred to in this Agreement shall take place;
“Application” the application to which the Council gave the reference
20/75239/FUL for full planning permission for the demolition of existing buildings and
the erection of a mixed-use development comprising of two ground floor commercial
units (open Use Classes A1, A2, A3, or B1) and 38 (thirty eight) apartments together
with parking and servicing at lower ground floor level;
“Bed Space” calculated in accordance with the provisions of the SPD on the basis
that the number of bed spaces in a Dwelling equals the number of bedrooms therein
plus one and “Bed Spaces” shall be construed accordingly;
“Commencement of Development” the date upon which the Development shall
begin by the carrying out of a material operation in accordance with the provisions of
section 56 (4) of the Act PROVIDED THAT any works of or associated with
demolition, site clearance, remediation works, environmental or archaeological
investigations, site and soil surveys, erections of contractors work compound,
erection of site office, erection of fencing to site boundaries, marking of site
boundaries and laying out of access roads and services shall for the purposes of this
Agreement not be deemed to be material operations and “Commence”,
“Commencement” and “Commenced” shall be construed accordingly;
“Completion of Construction” in respect of Dwellings, or a Block or Phase as
defined in Schedule 5, means the date upon which a valid certificate of completion
shall have been issued in respect of the relevant number of Dwellings, or the Block
or Phase for the purposes of the Building Act 1984 and the Building Regulations
2010 or any amendment or replacement of the same, or, if the Council, acting
reasonably, considers that the completion of construction of all of the Dwellings, or of
a Block or Phase as defined in Schedule 5, has occurred but it has not received the
notice confirming completion in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement
shall mean the date that the Council notifies in writing to the Owner that the said
completion of construction is to be deemed to have taken place for the purposes of
this Agreement and “Completed”, “Completion” and “Constructed” shall be
construed accordingly;
“Development” the development undertaken on the Site pursuant to the Planning
Permission as specified in the Application and “Developed” shall be construed
accordingly. If the development is undertaken on the Site in Phases (as defined in
this Agreement) then “Development” and “Developed” may be construed as
referring to the development undertaken on those Phases;
“Director” the Council’s Strategic Director Place or such other officer of the Council
as may from time to time be nominated in writing to act in place of the Council’s
Strategic Director Place;
“Duplex Unit” means:
(a) any Dwelling that consists of self-contained residential accommodation which
has direct access to it on the ground floor and “Duplex Units” shall be
construed accordingly;
(b) other forms of self-contained residential accommodation that would have a
similar function to the above category in (a) having regard to the size and
layout of their internal and external space, particularly in terms of the
likelihood of them being occupied by households with children and having
ground floor or podium access, and “Duplex Units” shall be construed
accordingly.
“Dwelling” a unit of accommodation to be constructed on the Site as part of the
Development pursuant to the Planning Permission;
“Expert” a professional expert in town planning, who is a Chartered Member of the
Royal Town Planning Institute with a minimum of ten (10) years post-qualification
experience;
“House” (a) a self contained Dwelling with direct access from the ground floor and
no adjoining accommodation either above or below, such as detached, semi
detached, terraced, townhouse and mews Dwellings, or; (b) other forms of self
contained Dwelling with a similar function to (a), having regard to the size and layout
of their internal and external space, particularly in terms of the likelihood of them
being occupied by households with children, such as, for example, Duplex Units; and
“Houses” shall be construed accordingly
“Index Linked” adjusted on an annual basis or pro rata for each day from the date
of this Agreement to the relevant due date for payment in accordance with the Retail
Price Index and “Index Linking” shall be construed accordingly;
“Interest” interest at 4% (four per cent) above the base lending rate of the Bank of
England from time to time;
"Monitoring Fee" in accordance with the power contained in the Community
Infrastructure Levy (Amendment) (England) (No.2) Regulations 2019 (as the same
may be amended or replaced) the Council charges an additional fee to cover the
cost of monitoring planning obligations. The amount charged equates to one and a
half per cent (1.5%) of the total value of the financial payments secured by this
Agreement, capped at a maximum of £5,000 where that total value would otherwise
exceed £5,000 and the Index Linked sum payable in accordance with the provisions
contained in Schedule 3 is calculated once the Maximum Contribution has been
calculated in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement. For the avoidance of
doubt when calculating the Monitoring Fee the fee is based upon the total value of
the financial payments that the Council has determined that the Development can
support and no viability related adjustments will be made. In this case the Index
Linked Monitoring Fee amounts to £1,863.06 (one thousand eight hundred and sixty
three pounds and six pence) Index Linked and payable in accordance with the
provisions contained in Schedule 3;
“Mortgagees” means together the First Mortgagee, Second Mortgagee, and Third
Mortgagee and “Mortgagee” shall be construed as meaning any of the Mortgagees;
“Occupation” means occupation of any part of the Development for the purposes
permitted by the Planning Permission but does not include use by personnel whilst
engaged in construction, fitting out or decoration of the Dwellings or occupation for
marketing or display or occupation in relation to security operations and “Occupy”
and “Occupied” shall be construed accordingly;
“Open Space Contribution” the sum of £1,637 (one thousand six hundred and
thirty seven pounds) per Bed Space for Houses and Index Linked and £1,182 (one
thousand one hundred and eighty two pounds) per Bed Space for apartments and
Index Linked to be paid in accordance with Policy H8 of the UDP and the provisions
of Policy OB2 of the SPD and directed towards the provision or improvement or
maintenance of public open space in the vicinity of the Site as more particularly
described in Schedule 4. In accordance with the SPD the amount payable is
£124,204 (one hundred and twenty four thousand two hundred and four pounds) and
Index Linked;
“Plan” the plan attached to the Agreement;
“Planning Permission” the planning permission granted pursuant to the Application
substantially in the form as appended at Schedule 2 and as may be amended by any
non-material amendment;
“Regulations” the Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010.
“Retail Price Index” twelve (12) month percentage change in the All Items Retail
Price Index published by the Office for National Statistics Centre and in the Monthly
Digest of Statistics (or contained in any official publication substituted therefor) or
such other index as may from time to time be published in substitution therefor;
“Site” the property described in Schedule 1 and shown for the purposes of
identification only edged red on the Plan;
“SPD” the City of Salford Council’s Supplementary Planning Document entitled
“Planning Obligations” (adopted 18 June 2015 and refreshed on 9 December 2019);
“Together Legal Charges” means two legal charges and two Debentures each
dated 3 October 2019 registered against all of the titles recited in the Background
section of this Agreement the beneficiary in respect of which is the First Mortgagee;
“UDP” the City of Salford Unitary Development Plan 2004-2016 (adopted 21 June
“Working Day” means any day except Saturday Sunday or a bank holiday and
reference to “Working Days” shall be construed accordingly.
1.2 The Clause headings do not affect this interpretation.
1.3 Unless otherwise indicated, references to Clauses and Schedules are to Clauses
of and Schedules to this Agreement and references in a Schedule to a Part or
Paragraph are to a Part or Paragraph of that Schedule.
1.4 References to any statute or statutory provision include reference to:
1.4.1 all Acts of Parliament and all other legislation having legal effect in the United
Kingdom as directly or indirectly amended, consolidated, extended, replaced or re
enacted by any subsequent legislation; and
1.4.2 any orders, regulations, instruments or other subordinate legislation made
under that statute or statutory provision.
1.5 Except for the provisions of Clause 9 references to the Site include any part of it.
1.6 Save in respect of clause 19.2 references to any party in this Agreement include
the successors in title of that party. In addition, references to the Council include any
successor local planning authority exercising planning powers under the Act and any
successor local highway authority exercising powers under the Highways Act 1980.
1.7 “Including” means “including, without limitation”.
1.8 Any covenant by the Owner or the Council not to do any act or thing includes a
covenant not to permit or allow the doing of that act or thing.
1.9 If any provision is held to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable, the legality, validity
and enforceability of the remainder of this Agreement is to be unaffected.
1.10 Words importing the singular meaning where the context so admits include the
plural meaning and vice versa.
1.11 Words of the masculine gender include the feminine and neuter genders and
words denoting actual persons include companies, corporations and firms and all
such words shall be construed interchangeable in that manner.
2 Planning Obligation
This Agreement is made pursuant to section 106 of the Act, section 111 of the Local
Government Act 1972, section 1 of the Localism Act 2011 and all other enabling
legislation and is a planning obligation for the purposes of section 106 of the Act,
with the intent that covenants hereinafter contained shall be enforceable by the
Council acting under the powers contained in section 106 or such other enabling
powers against the Owner.
3 Condition Precedent
3.1 This Agreement is conditional upon the grant of the Planning Permission save for
the provisions of Clauses 9, 11, 15, 17, and 18 which shall have immediate effect.
4 Condition Subsequent
If the Planning Permission for the Development has not been implemented by the
carrying out of a material operation in accordance with the provisions of sections 56,
91 and 93 of the Act or is revoked or modified in whole or in part (other than in
approval of an application by or on behalf of either of the Owner) or quashed or
declared unlawful as a result of legal proceedings then this Agreement shall
absolutely determine and become null and void but without prejudice to the rights of
either party against the other in respect of any antecedent breach.
5 The Owner’s Covenants
5.1 The Owner on behalf of itself and any person deriving title to any part of the Site
from the Owner hereafter hereby covenants with the Council so as to bind the Site to
fully observe and perform the obligations on its part contained in this Agreement
including those obligations set out in Schedule 3 and Schedule 5 and hereby agrees
that the Site shall be permanently subject to the obligations, restrictions and
provisions specified herein, such obligations being planning obligations for the
purpose of section 106 of the Act save that this Agreement shall not be enforceable
against i) owner-occupiers or tenants of the Dwellings (or those areas of the
Development which are not Dwellings) constructed pursuant to the Planning
Permission nor against those deriving title from them and ii) statutory undertakers or
service/utility providers providing their services to the Site.
6 The Council’s Covenants
The Council hereby covenants with the Owner to observe and perform the
obligations on its part in this Agreement including those obligations set out in the
Schedule 4.
7 Dispute Resolution
7.1 In the event of any dispute arising in connection with any of the terms of this
Agreement other than a dispute involving the construction or interpretation of the
terms of this Agreement or the enforcement of any decision pursuant to this Clause,
the same shall unless the Council and the Owner otherwise agree be referred to an
Expert to be appointed by agreement between the Council and the Owner.
7.2 If the Council and the Owner are unable to agree on the appointment of an
Expert within thirty (30) days of one party serving notice on the other calling for the
appointment of an Expert, then an Expert shall be appointed on the application of
either party to the President for the time being of the Royal Town Planning Institute.
7.3 Any reference of a dispute to an Expert shall if the parties are agreed in writing
be deemed to be a reference to an expert or chartered surveyor (and not to an
arbitrator) whose decision shall be final and binding (save for manifest error) but
shall otherwise be deemed to be a reference to an arbitrator pursuant to the
Arbitration Act 1996 and any statutory amendment variation substitution or re
enactment thereof.
7.4 Any party to this Agreement shall be entitled to submit to the Expert
representations and cross-representations with such supporting evidence as they
shall respectively consider necessary and the Expert shall have regard thereto in
making his decision which shall be delivered in writing. The reference of any dispute
shall include authority to determine in what manner all the costs of the referral shall
be paid.
8 Waiver
No waiver (whether expressed or implied) by the Council of any breach or default in
performing or observing any of the covenants terms or conditions of this Agreement
shall constitute a continuing waiver and no such waiver shall prevent the Council
from enforcing any of the relevant terms or conditions or from acting upon any
subsequent breach or default.
9 Change in Ownership & Liability
9.1 The Owner agrees with the Council to give the Council immediate written notice
of any change in Ownership of any of its interest in the Site occurring before all the
obligations under this Agreement have been discharged such notice to give details of
the transferee’s full name and registered office (if a company or usual address if not)
together with (unless the purchase relates to the entirety of the Site) the area of the
Site or unit of occupation purchased by reference to a plan.
9.2 No person shall be liable for any breach, non performance and non observance
of the covenants, obligations and restrictions contained in this Agreement after it
shall have parted with its entire interest in the Site but without prejudice to liability for
any subsisting breach arising prior to parting with such interest nor shall this hinder
or preclude the Council’s rights as the Local Planning Authority to require that the
breach, non performance or non observance be remedied after that person has
parted with its interest in the Site.
9.3 The Owner warrants that no person other than the Owner and the Mortgagees
has any legal or equitable interest in the Site and the Owner hereby indemnifies the
Council in respect of any loss that arises should there be any breach of this
warranty.
10 Council’s Consent Or Approval
Where in this Agreement the consent, agreement or approval of the Council is
required to be given by the Council, the Council confirms that such consent,
agreement or approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed provided that
this shall not fetter the proper discretion of the Council.
11 Local Land Charge And Land Registry Entry
11.1 This Agreement is a Local Land Charge and shall be registered as such by the
Council.
11.2 For the purpose of noting this Agreement on the titles of the Owner registered
under title numbers GM813338, LA103094, GM388032 and MAN332903 at the
Land Registry the Owner will on the date hereof provide the Council with completed
Form AN1 (or any replacement of this form) together with either a cheque made
payable to the Land Registry to cover the requisite fee or alternatively with the
Owner’s solicitor’s completed Land Registry account key number details inserted in
the form. The Council will arrange for the AN1 (or any replacement of this form) to
be registered at the Land Registry and the Owner will supply the Council with a copy
of the amended registers as soon as reasonably practicable following their receipt by
the Owner from the Land Registry.
11.3 The Council will upon receipt of a written request of the Owner or its successors
in title, at any time after the obligations set out herein have been fulfilled in their
entirety, issue written confirmation thereon and thereafter cancel all related entries in
the register of local land charges.
11.4 The costs of registration and cancellation pursuant to clauses 11.3 above shall
be met by the Owner if requested by the Council.
12 Non-Prohibition on Development
Nothing in this Agreement shall prohibit or limit the right to develop any part of the
Site in accordance with a planning permission (other than the Planning Permission
granted (whether or not on appeal) after the date of this Agreement.
13 The Contracts Act
Save as provided in respect of the successors in title to the Site or any successor to
the relevant statutory functions of the Council this Agreement shall not be
enforceable by any third party pursuant to the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act
1999 and no third party shall acquire any benefit rights or claims whatsoever
pursuant thereto.
14 Communication
14.1 Any notice or document to be served on or sent pursuant to this Agreement
shall either be delivered personally or sent by recorded delivery service
14.1.1 to the Council and addressed to the Director at the Council’s address first
above written;
14.1.2 to the First Owner, the Second Owner, the Developer and the Mortgagee
respectively at their registered office address;
15 Fees
15.1 The Owner shall pay forthwith to the Council its legal fees reasonably and
properly incurred in preparation of this Agreement;
15.2 Receipt by the Council of the payment of such sum shall not create any lawyer
client type contractual relationship between the Council and the Owner nor absolve
the Owner from any liability or obligation imposed upon them by the terms of this
Agreement or by statute or at common law;
15.4 The Owner shall on the date set out in Schedule 3 pay to the Council the
Monitoring Fee.
16. Interest
If any payment due under this Agreement is paid late Interest will be payable from
the date payment is due to the date that payment is received.
17. Jurisdiction
This Agreement is governed by and interpreted in accordance with the law of
England.
18 Completion
The provisions of this Agreement (other than this clause which shall be of immediate
effect) shall be of no effect until this Agreement has been dated.
19 Mortgagees
19.1 The Mortgagees consent to this Agreement being entered into with the intention
that their interests in the Site in the form of the Together Legal Charges, the Second
Mortgagee’s Charges, and the Third Mortgagee’s Charges will be bound by the
terms of this Agreement as if this Agreement had been executed and registered as a
local land charge before their execution.
19.2 Notwithstanding clause 19.1, a Mortgagee will not incur any liability for any
breach of the obligations contained in this Agreement unless they are committed
whilst it is a mortgagee in possession of the Site or any part of it. For the avoidance
of doubt the provision contained in this clause 19.2 does not apply to any successor
in title to a Mortgagee.
20 Restriction
The Owner covenants with the Council:
20.1 that prior to or upon completion of this Agreement the Owner shall provide
the Council with a completed Land Registry form RX1 (or any subsequent
revisions amendments or replacements of the same) signed by the Owner
and thereby authorising the Council to register a restriction in standard form L
at the Land Registry in respect of the titles comprising the Owner’s’ interest in
the Site in the following terms:
“No disposition of the registered estate (other than a charge) by the proprietor of the
registered estate is to be registered without a certificate signed by Manchester City
Council, Town Hall, Albert Square, Manchester, M60 2LA that the provisions of
Schedules 3 and 5 of a Section 106 Agreement dated
made between (1) The Council of the City of Salford (2) Hilton Street Developments
(Manchester) Limited (3) Together Commercial Finance Limited (4) ECS Capital
Limited and Andrew Higginson and (5) ECS Capital Limited and Apple P.P.E.
Limited have been complied with or that they do not apply to the disposition.”
The Council will insert the date of completion of this Agreement into the section of
the Form RX1 detailing the wording quoted above following that completion;
20.2. to be responsible for the costs of registering the RX1 form referred to in
clause 20.1 immediately above.
EXECUTED as a deed by the parties on the day and year first hereinbefore
appearing.
Schedule 1
The Site
Land at 311-315 Bury New Road, Salford, M7 2YN and shown for the purposes of
identification only edged red on the Plan.
Schedule 2
Draft Planning Permission
Schedule 3
The Owner’s General Covenants
The Owner hereby covenants with the Council as follows:
1. To notify the Council in writing:
1.1 at least 14 (fourteen) Working Days in advance of the Anticipated date of
Commencement of Development;
1.2 within 5 (five) Working Days of their occurrence of Commencement of
Development.
2. To pay to the Council the Open Space Contribution on or before
Commencement of Development and at the same time to pay to the Council
the Monitoring Fee.
Schedule 4
The Council’s Covenants
The Council hereby covenants with the Owner as follows:
1 To use any Affordable Housing Contribution it receives for the provision of
Affordable Housing within the Administrative Boundaries of Salford and for no
other purpose.
2 To use the Open Space Contribution when received at the Council’s sole
discretion as follows:
2.1 towards improvements to Albert Park and/or
2.2 towards improvements to Green Grosvenor Park.
3 At the written request of the Owner to provide written confirmation of the
discharge of the obligations contained in this Agreement when satisfied that
such obligations have been performed.
4 At the written request of the Owner the Council shall repay to the person who
first paid to the Council such payment any balance of the Open Space
Contribution and of any Affordable Housing Contribution that the Council has
received (excluding any such sums in respect of which though not yet
expended the Council has contractually committed to expend) and any
interest thereon that remains unexpended 10 (ten) years from the date of the
receipt of payment (the “retention period”) to the Council of the latest payment
that the Council has received or in the case of monies allocated to
maintenance 20 (twenty) years from such date.
5 Upon receipt by the Council of a written request from the Owner received
within the final year of the retention period of the payment of the Open Space
Contribution or if received of any Affordable Housing Contribution to provide a
written statement summarising what the payments have been spent on and
detailing any sums remaining unexpended within 21 days of such request
provided that the number of such requests shall not exceed four.
6 To issue the Planning Permission within two (2) Working Days of the date
hereof.
Schedule 5
Additional Definitions And Covenants Relating To Affordable Housing
Definitions
“Affordable Housing” affordable housing as defined in the National Planning Policy
Framework (NPPF) issued in June 2019 (as may be updated or replaced with an
equivalent policy from time to time) that will be available to persons who cannot
afford to rent or buy housing generally available on the open market provided that
the total amount of Affordable Housing Units on the Site shall be three Units as
specified in Paragraph 1.2 of this Schedule.
“Affordable Housing Contribution” an Index Linked sum equivalent to the cost to
the Owner of providing the number, size and type of Affordable Housing Units on the
Site as would be required under policies H1 and H4 of the UDP and policy OB1 of
the SPD such sum to be calculated for any Affordable Housing Units approved by
the Council under the Affordable Housing Scheme in respect of which an Affordable
Housing Contribution becomes payable in accordance with the provisions of this
Agreement by multiplying each of those Affordable Housing Units by the Relevant
Discount applicable to those Affordable Housing Units.
“Affordable Housing Scheme” a written scheme to be submitted to and approved
in writing by the Council for the provision of three Affordable Housing Units on the
Site in accordance with policies H1 and H4 of the UDP and detailing the size,
location, occupancy criteria and tenure mix of those three Affordable Housing Units,
together with the composition of any Intermediate Housing Units, on the Site as a
whole.
“Affordable Housing Units” those Dwellings which shall be designated as
Affordable Housing under the Affordable Housing Scheme submitted by the Owner
and approved by the Council and in accordance with the Planning Permission and to
be constructed according to the quality and design standards of the Regulator and
“Units” shall be construed accordingly.
“Block” a single building that contains Dwellings that will be erected as part of the
Development and “Blocks” shall be construed accordingly.
“Chargee” shall mean any mortgagee, chargee or other financial institution of the
Registered Provider or a Security Trustee or receiver or manager (including an
administrative receiver) appointed pursuant to the Law of Property Act 1925 or any
successors in title thereof.
“Chargee’s Duty” the tasks and duties set out in paragraph 9 of this Schedule.
“HE” Homes England or the Regulator of Social Housing established under the
Housing and Regeneration Act 2008 or such other body as may replace them for the
purpose of procuring and regulating Affordable Housing from time to time and
“Homes England” shall be construed accordingly.
“Initial Sale Percentage” the percentage of the equity in an Affordable Housing Unit
purchased by an occupier upon entering into a Shared Equity Arrangement.
“Intermediate Housing Unit” any Affordable Housing Unit to be constructed to the
same overall standard in terms of quality and finish as a comparable Market Housing
Unit and disposed of at a cost below market levels, under either a Shared Ownership
Lease or Shared Equity Arrangement in accordance with the relevant provisions of
the Housing and Regeneration Act 2008 and marketed in accordance with guidance
issued by HE (or successor body) from time to time and “Intermediate Housing
Units” and “Intermediate Housing” shall be construed accordingly.
“Market Housing Unit” that part of the Development which is general market
housing for sale on the open market and which is not Affordable Housing.
“NPPF” the National Planning Policy Framework issued in June 2019 being the
framework setting out the Government’s planning policies for England and how these
are expected to be applied as may be amended or any replacement of the same.
“Open Market Value” the estimated amount for which the Affordable Housing Units
would be sold on the open market as Market Housing Units between a willing buyer
and a willing seller in an arm’s length transaction after proper marketing wherein the
parties had each acted knowledgeably, prudently and without compulsion.
“Phase” shall mean if the Planning Permission or any related reserved matters
approvals by the Council allow for the carrying out of the Development in distinct
phases any such phase of the Development and “Phases”, and “Phase of the
Development” shall be construed accordingly.
“Practical Completion” issue of a certificate of practical completion by the Owner's
architect or in the event that the Development is constructed by a party other than
the Owner the issue of a certificate of practical completion by that other party’s
architect.
“Protected Tenant” any tenant who:
(a) has exercised the right to acquire pursuant to the Housing and Regeneration
Act 2008 or any statutory provision for the time being in force (or any
equivalent contractual right) in respect of a particular Affordable Housing Unit;
(b) has exercised any statutory right to buy (or any equivalent contractual right) in
respect of a particular Affordable Housing Unit;
(c) has entered into a Shared Equity Arrangement with a Registered Provider (or
similar arrangement where a share of the Affordable Housing Unit is owned
by the tenant and a share is owned by the Registered Provider) in respect of a
particular Affordable Housing Unit and the tenant has subsequently
purchased from the Registered Provider all the remaining equity so that the
tenant owns the entire Affordable Housing Unit.
“Registered Provider” or “RP” a registered provider as defined in the Housing and
Regeneration Act 2008 or any replacement, amendment or revision of the same who
is registered with Homes England.
“Regulator of Social Housing” means the body established under the Housing and
Regeneration Act 2008 as amended by the Legislative Reform (Regulator of Social
Housing) (England) Order 2018/1040 or such other body as may replace them for
the purpose of regulating Affordable Housing from time to time and “Regulator” shall
be construed accordingly.
“Relevant Discount” the percentage of Open Market Value to be applied to each
tenure type of Affordable Housing Unit, such sums to be:
30% of Open Market Value for Affordable Housing Units disposed of under a Shared
Ownership Lease or Shared Equity Arrangement.
“Right to Acquire” the right of a tenant to acquire the Affordable Housing Unit of
which they are a tenant provided for under section 180 of the Housing and
Regeneration Act 2008 and governed by the Housing Act 1985 and modified by the
Housing (Right to Acquire) Regulations 1997 as the same may be modified or as
contained in any replacement of the same.
“Right to Buy” the right of a tenant to buy the Affordable Housing Unit of which they
are a tenant provided:
(a) under the Housing Act 1985 and under the Housing and Planning Act 2016 as
the same may be modified or as contained in any replacement of the same, or
(b) any equivalent contractual right,
(c) any extension of the Right to Buy to tenants of Registered Providers either
through a voluntary scheme brought in by a Registered Provider or by government
legislation as the same may be modified or contained in any replacement of the
same.
“Shared Equity Arrangement” arrangements which provide for ownership to be
shared between the occupier and a landlord under which the occupier owns part of
the equity and pays to the landlord an annual fee of no more than 3% (three per
cent) of the value of the part of the equity retained by the landlord. Such ownership
by the occupier shall:
(a) initially not be less than 10% (ten per cent) or more than 75% (seventy
five per cent) of the equity when measured against full Open Market
Value of the relevant Affordable Housing Unit;
(b) include the entitlement from time to time to Staircase upwards from the
Initial Sale Percentage towards a pre-determined maximum percentage
(which shall be up to 100% (one hundred per cent) in respect of his or
her share of the full Open Market Value of the Affordable Housing
Unit).
“Shared Ownership Lease” a lease the terms of which provide for ownership to be
shared between the occupier and a landlord under which the occupier owns part of
the equity in the leasehold title and pays a rental on the balance of the equity held in
the leasehold interest. Such ownership by the occupier shall not be more than 75%
(seventy five per cent) of the equity when measured against full Open Market Value
of the relevant Affordable Housing Unit and “Shared Ownership” shall be construed
accordingly.
“Sold” means where the Owner has transferred ownership of a Dwelling to another
person or body or created any form of tenancy or licence relating to a Dwelling
whereby a tenant or licensee may Occupy that Dwelling and “Sale” shall be
construed accordingly.
“Staircasing” the exercise of the right of a purchaser under a Shared Equity
Arrangement to increase their ownership in an Affordable Housing Unit up to 100%
of the equity in the Affordable Housing Unit and “Staircase” shall be construed
accordingly.
“Staircasing Receipts and Other Affordable Housing Receipts” any receipts
received by the Owner following disposal arising from Right to Buy, Right to Acquire
(or equivalent) or arising in respect of a Shared Ownership Lease as a result of
Staircasing by the tenant.
Covenants
The Owner hereby covenants with the Council as follows:
1. Prior to Commencement of Development on the Site or if Developed in
Phases in any Phase to submit to the Council for its written approval the
Affordable Housing Scheme for the Site or if applicable for that Phase in
writing, such scheme to detail the following:
1.1. (unless otherwise agreed) three of the total number of Dwellings
approved under the Planning Permission for the Development of the
Site as a whole or when aggregated over all Phases to be Affordable
Housing Units;
1.2. (unless otherwise agreed) the Affordable Housing Units will consist of 1
x 1 bed apartments and 2 x 2 bed apartments.
1.3. That all the Affordable Housing to be provided on the Site or if
applicable in that Phase shall be Intermediate Housing Shared
Ownership tenure and:
1.3.1. the three Affordable Housing Units will be disposed of under a
Shared Ownership Lease;
1.4. detailed plans showing the locations of Affordable Housing Units to be
provided within the Site or if applicable that Phase, such locations to
ensure tenure blind design and full integration (“pepper-potted”) with
the Market Housing Units generally within the Site or if applicable that
Phase;
1.5. the arrangements to be put in place to ensure that the Affordable
Housing Units are affordable for both initial and subsequent occupiers;
1.6. the occupancy criteria to be used for determining the identity of
prospective and successive occupiers of the Affordable Housing Units
and the means by which such occupancy shall be enforced.
2. Not to Commence Development on the Site or if applicable on any Phase until
the Affordable Housing Scheme for the Site or if applicable for that Phase has
been submitted to and approved in writing by the Council.
3. To provide the Affordable Housing in accordance with the approved
Affordable Housing Scheme/s.
4. Prior to Commencement of Development on the Site or if applicable in any
Phase, to make offers to sell the Affordable Housing Units in the Site or if
applicable in that Phase at a discounted price that will support the delivery of
Affordable Housing on Site in accordance with the approved Affordable
Housing Scheme for the Site or if applicable for that Phase to a minimum of 2
(two) RPs, such RPs to be agreed by the prior written approval of the Council.
5. In the event of the earlier of:
5.1. all RPs to whom offers in accordance with Paragraph 4 are made
declining to accept the transfer of the Affordable Housing Units in
accordance with the offer or offers made to it; or
5.2. Six (6) months expiring from the date of receipt of the latest of any
detailed offer documentation by the RPs received without a binding
acceptance of an offer made by any of them within that period; then the
Owner shall pay to the Council the Affordable Housing Contribution in
the following instalments:
5.2.1. Where the Development is completed in Blocks or Phases the
first instalment representing the Affordable Housing Contribution
due in respect of any Affordable Housing Unit contained in the
first Block or Phase will be payable on Completion of
Construction of all of the Dwellings comprised in the first Block
or Phase to be Completed. Where the Development is not
Completed in Blocks or Phases then 50% (fifty per cent) of the
Affordable Housing Contribution is payable when 30% (thirty per
cent) of the Dwellings on the Site have been Sold; and
5.2.2. Where the Development is completed in Blocks or Phases the
second instalment representing the Affordable Housing
Contribution due in respect of any Affordable Housing Unit
contained in the second Block or Phase to be Completed or if
more than two Blocks or Phases in the last Block or Phase to be
Completed, will be payable on Completion of Construction of all
of the Dwellings comprised in that Block or Phase. Where the
Development is not Completed in Blocks or Phases then 50%
(fifty per cent) of the Affordable Housing Contribution is payable
when 50% (fifty per cent) of the Dwellings on the Site have been
Sold; and
5.2.3 the Affordable Housing Contribution is to be calculated:
5.2.3.1 in respect of 5.2.1 if the Development is Completed in Blocks or
Phases on the date when Completion of Construction of all of the
Dwellings comprised in the first Block or Phase to be Completed takes
place and if not Completed in Blocks or Phases on the date that 30%
(thirty per cent) of the Dwellings on the Site or in that Phase (as
appropriate) have been Sold; and
5.2.3.2 in respect of 5.2.2 if the Development is Completed in Blocks or
Phases on the date when Completion of Construction of all of the
Dwellings contained in the second Block or Phase to be Completed, or
if more than two Blocks or Phases in the last Block or Phase to be
Completed, takes place and if not Completed in Blocks or Phases on
the date that 50% (fifty per cent) of the Dwellings on the Site have been
Sold;
5.3 In respect of whichever of such events will take place, at least 10 (ten)
Working Days before the anticipated dates of Completion of Construction of
the first Block or Phase to be Completed, Completion of Construction of the
last Block or Phase to be Completed, and the completion of the Sale of 30%
and of 50% of the Dwellings, to notify the Council of those anticipated dates;
5.4 In respect of whichever of such events will take place, within 5 (five) Working
Days of the dates of Completion of Construction of the first Block or Phase to
be Completed, Completion of Construction of the last Block or Phase to be
Completed, and the completion of the Sale of 30% and 50% of the Dwellings
to notify the Council in writing of those dates.
6. Not to allow Occupation of more than 30% (thirty per cent) of the Dwellings
comprised in the first Block or Phase to be Completed, or where the
Development does not comprise of Blocks or Phases, of more than 30%
(thirty per cent) of the Market Housing Units on the Site until the first
Affordable Housing Unit on the Site or in that Block or Phase (as appropriate)
has been completed in accordance with the Planning Permission and the
Affordable Housing Scheme and made ready for Occupation and transferred
to a RP and written notification of such has been given to the Council or the
Owner has paid the relevant amount of Affordable Housing Contribution as
set out in paragraph 5.2.1 above.
7. Not to allow Occupation of more than 50% of the Dwellings contained in the
last of any remaining Blocks or Phases to be Completed, or where the
Development does not comprise of Blocks or Phases, of more than 50% (fifty
per cent) of the Market Housing Units on the Site until all of the Affordable
Housing Units have been completed in accordance with the Planning
Permission and the Affordable Housing Scheme and made ready for
Occupation and transferred to an RP and written notification of such has been
given to the Council or the Owner has paid the relevant amount of Affordable
Housing Contribution as set out in paragraph 5.2.2 above.
8. From the date of Practical Completion of the Affordable Housing Units they
shall not be used other than for Affordable Housing save that this obligation
shall not be binding on:
8.1. any Protected Tenant or any mortgagee or chargee of the Protected
Tenant or any person deriving title from the Protected Tenant or any
successor in title thereto and their respective mortgagees and
chargees; or
8.2. any Chargee provided that the Chargee shall have first complied with
the Chargee’s Duty and any person deriving title from the Chargee or
any successor in title thereto and their respective mortgagees and
chargees; or
8.3. any purchaser from a mortgagee of an individual Affordable Housing
Unit pursuant to any default by the individual mortgagor and any
person deriving title from that purchaser or any successor in title
thereto and their respective mortgagees and chargees.
9. The Chargee shall prior to seeking to dispose of the Affordable Housing Units
pursuant to any default under the terms of its mortgage or charge give not
less than one month’s prior notice (“Chargee’s Notice”) to the Council of its
intention to dispose and:
9.1 in the event that the Council responds within one month from receipt of
the Chargee’s Notice (“the Council’s Notice”) indicating that
arrangements for the transfer of the Affordable Housing Units can be
made in such a way as to safeguard them as Affordable Housing and
that will satisfy the terms of the mortgage or charge then the Chargee
shall co-operate with such arrangements and use its reasonable
endeavours to secure such transfer; or
9.2 if the Council does not serve its response to the Chargee’s Notice
within the one month period referred to above at paragraph 9.1 then
the Chargee shall be entitled to dispose of the Affordable Housing
Units or any part thereof free from the restrictions set out in this
Schedule; or
9.3 if the Council or any person nominated by the Council cannot within
two months of receipt of the Council’s Notice secure completion of
such transfer (so that for the avoidance of doubt there shall be a total
of only 3 months from the Chargee’s Notice to completion of such
transfer) then provided the Chargee shall have complied with its
obligations under paragraph 9.1 the Chargee shall be entitled to
dispose of the Affordable Housing Units or any part thereof free from
the restrictions set out in this Schedule.
9.4 provided that at all times the rights and obligations in this paragraph 9
shall not require the Chargee to act contrary to its duties under the
charge or mortgage and in particular (but without limitation):
9.4.1 the Chargee shall not be obliged to transfer, let or otherwise dispose of the
Affordable Housing Units or any part thereof for a consideration less than the full
amount outstanding under the legal charge or mortgage, plus all interest, costs and
expenses.
10. Unless required by the HE to do otherwise not to use any Staircasing
Receipts and Other Affordable Housing Receipts other than towards the
provision of Affordable Housing within the Administrative Boundaries of
Salford.
